defect.evidence_quote: When a law enforcement officer claims authority to search a home under a warrant, he announces in effect that the occupant has no right to resist the search. The situation is instinct with coercion — albeit colorably lawful coercion. Where there is coercion there cannot be consent.
defect.problem: The black-letter rule is only partly supported by the disclosed lake records. The disclosed pinpoints support voluntariness/totality, common authority, and objective scope, but no disclosed text verifies the preponderance standard, and the quoted Bumper sentence at 548-549 is not present in the Bumper lake pinpoints. With no text/ opinion file, quote fidelity and that burden standard cannot be verified from disclosed evidence.
defect.proposed_fix: Add a disclosed authority/pinpoint for the preponderance burden and add the exact Bumper 548-549 text to the lake pinpoints or remove/replace the quotation with a disclosed quote such as Bumper pin-550.

reasons: Schneckloth pin-227 supports voluntariness judged on totality and no required knowledge of right to refuse.
Matlock pin-171 supports third-party common authority over premises or effects; Jimeno pin-251 supports objective scope for car-for-narcotics consent.

A disclosed-file search found no lake occurrence of preponderance/preponderant, and Bumper pin-548/pin-550 do not contain the exact quoted sentence: "cannot be discharged by showing no more than acquiescence to a claim of lawful authority."
residual_risks: The rule may be legally correct if full opinion text or another authority were added, but it is not verifiable from the disclosed files as framed.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Separate the three-prong rule from the burden-standard sentence, and pin each component to disclosed authority; use only verbatim quotes present in text/ or lake pinpoints.
